meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Hale. Was Owen heard before you entered that zero?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. What do you have?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. He wrote it over the weekend and pasted it in, and that is what a paste looks like. Did you speak to Owen before the zero went in, yes or no?
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Pull it up. And I asked you a yes or no about Owen; I'll take no answer as a no.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
A wrong quotation is a wrong quotation. Seventeen-year-olds copy bad lines off study sites every day. And your screen is still facing you, Hale.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
So he changed his mind after October 15. That's called thinking. Hand me both.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
So you did speak to him, November 2. "Like, being stuck" is what paralysis means. Was that in front of his class?
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in a classroom against a weekend at home with the book open. You skipped my question. November 2, in front of his class or not?
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Good. 4.3 says you can't. Is anything on Owen's record right now?
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.

That's 4.4. Owen does the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything, and it's private, away from his class, and marked before December 1. I'll want that in an email tonight, with a line confirming nothing is on his record now.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Ten minutes. It works if the email reaches me tonight and the new mark is in before December 1. Which day does he write it?
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Thursday, November 12. Put that in tonight's email with the rest.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
Thursday, November 12, and nothing on his record now or later. Then yes.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
Copies of what you described today, attached to that email. And who else has seen any of this, Hale?
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

In today's meeting you agreed to a private supervised rewrite for Owen on Thursday, November 12, away from his class, with the new mark replacing the zero well before December 1 and nothing placed on his record. I still require copies of every document you described, a line confirming that nothing is on his record now, and an answer to my question about who else has seen any of this. You said I would have this in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: last position. She agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12 that replaces the zero with nothing on his record, and she still wants copies of your documents, confirmation that his record is clean now, and to know who else has seen this. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out.
What moved her: your same-day note of the November 2 conversation with Owen, because it was dated, about his own work, and showed he was heard before the zero went in.
What cost ground: moving to the next piece of evidence each time she asked a direct question, because she had to ask twice whether Owen was heard and twice whether he was questioned in front of his class, and each skipped answer made her sharper.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history put the whole essay arriving between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM on Wednesday, October 28, which is about as close to that night as evidence could come. It proves nothing about the essay; it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she said he wrote it over the weekend and pasted it in, turn the screen and answer that defence before going on to the quotation.
